result.answer:
Verdict: REFUTED

The paper describes the NYT evaluation as limited-length recall-based ROUGE in which the predicted summaries were truncated **to the length of the gold summaries**, not to one shared fixed length [S:0fc8fd43b7f1#3]. So truncation was tied to each article's own reference summary, which directly contradicts the claim that a single fixed length applied to all articles irrespective of their references [S:0fc8fd43b7f1#3]. The paper gives no indication of a uniform, reference-independent cutoff; the only length it names as a truncation target is the gold-summary length [S:0fc8fd43b7f1#3].

claims.text: The paper states that for NYT it adopted limited-length recall-based ROUGE and truncated predicted summaries to the length of the gold summaries.
claims.note: Span states adoption of limited-length recall-based ROUGE with truncation of predicted summaries to gold length for NYT.

claims.text: The paper reports NYT dataset results in its Table TABREF26.
claims.note: Span explicitly says Table TABREF26 presents results on NYT dataset.

claims.text: The paper reports gains on CNN/DailyMail and New York Times of 0.8 and 2.4 ROUGE-2 respectively over the best published abstractive model.
claims.note: Span gives 0.8 ROUGE-2 on CNN/DailyMail and 2.4 on New York Times over best published abstractive model, but the 0.8 is attributed to CNN/DailyMail rather than combined CNN/DailyMail wording; core numbers match.

extractive and abstractive models, respectively. Results of Step are listed in the third block. Similar to

models in Table TABREF26.
